title: Chinese Peanut Sauce Noodles
subtitle: Cold wheat noodles tossed with a peanut-sesame sauce and shredded chicken
excerpt: Cold noodles dressed in a nutty, tangy peanut-sesame sauce work as a starter or a main and hold up well in the fridge for a day. The sauce comes together in minutes while the noodles cook. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Cold peanut noodles (hua sheng jiang mian) are part of a broader Chinese tradition of liang mian (cold noodles) served in summer, found across Sichuan, Beijing, and Shanghainese cooking with regional variations in sauce composition. The peanut-sesame base reflects the same flavour logic as dan dan mian and sesame noodles, and has been documented in Chinese cookbooks since at least the early 20th century. The dish entered Western awareness through 1970s-80s Chinese-American restaurant culture and remains one of the most widely eaten Chinese noodle preparations globally.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Noodles dressed in sauce keep for 1 day -- toss with a splash of sesame oil before serving if they clump.

content.text: This serves 4 and takes about 25 minutes. The sauce is built around two nutty elements -- peanut butter and
sesame paste
-- loosened with soy sauce,
rice vinegar
, and a little hot water to reach a consistency that coats
wheat noodles
without clumping. The whole dish is served cold or at room temperature.

The key to cold noodles that do not stick is rinsing them immediately under cold water after cooking and tossing with a little sesame oil before dressing. This stops the starches from binding to each other. Dress the noodles no more than 30 minutes before serving, otherwise the sauce absorbs into the noodles and the dish dries out.
What you need
Method

Poach the chicken: place the chicken breast in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring to the boil, then immediately reduce to the lowest possible simmer. Cover and cook for 12-15 minutes. Remove, cool for 5 minutes, then shred with two forks along the grain of the meat.

Make the sauce. Whisk together the peanut butter and sesame paste, then add the hot water a tablespoon at a time, stirring until smooth and pourable. Add the light soy, rice vinegar, chilli oil, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, and sugar. Whisk until combined. Taste -- the sauce should be nutty, sharp, slightly sweet, and have a distinct chilli warmth. Adjust any element as needed.
Cook the wheat noodles in a large pan of boiling water according to the packet instructions. Drain immediately and rinse under cold running water until completely cool.
Shake the noodles dry and toss with a few drops of sesame oil to prevent sticking. Transfer to a large serving bowl or individual bowls.
Spoon the sauce over the noodles and toss to coat. Add the shredded chicken and cucumber matchsticks. Finish with
chilli oil
, sliced spring onions, and chopped roasted peanuts. Serve at room temperature.
If serving later, keep the sauce and noodles separate in the fridge and dress just before eating. Extra sauce can be stored in a jar in the fridge for up to 3 days.

items.symptom: Noodles have clumped into a solid mass
items.cause: Not rinsed thoroughly or not tossed with oil after draining
items.fix: Rinse under cold water for a full 30 seconds until completely cool, then toss with sesame oil immediately. If already clumped, pour boiling water over them to loosen, then rinse cold again.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thick to coat the noodles
items.cause: Peanut butter or sesame paste was stiff and not sufficiently loosened
items.fix: Whisk in hot water a tablespoon at a time until the sauce flows easily. It should coat the back of a spoon but not hold its shape.

items.symptom: Dish tastes flat despite following the sauce recipe
items.cause: Undersalted, or the vinegar/chilli balance is off for the batch of ingredients
items.fix: Taste the finished dish and adjust: more soy for salt, more rice vinegar for brightness, more chilli oil for heat. Cold dishes need slightly more seasoning than warm ones.

content.text: Where this dish lives

Cold peanut noodles are a summer dish eaten across China. Cook the noodles ahead and keep them chilled. The sauce can be made a few days in advance and kept in the fridge. Thin it with water if it thickens. Add shredded chicken, cucumber, or blanched green beans on top.
